kept.q: Which of the following physical quantities is a fundamental (base) quantity in the SI system of units?
kept.explanation: The seven SI base quantities are length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity. Force, energy and pressure are all derived from these base quantities, but electric current (ampere) is itself a base quantity.
kept.pidgin: SI get seven base quantities: length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity. Force, energy and pressure na derived ones, but current (ampere) na base quantity straight.

kept.q: The dimension of power (the rate of doing work) in terms of mass [M], length [L] and time [T] is:
kept.explanation: Work has dimension [M][L]^2[T]^-2 and power = work/time, so we divide by [T] to get [M][L]^2[T]^-3. This matches the SI unit watt, which equals joule per second.
kept.pidgin: Work get dimension [M][L]^2[T]^-2, and power na work divide by time, so you add one more [T]^-1 make e be [M][L]^2[T]^-3. Na so watt (joule per second) dimension be.

kept.q: A block of local 'iroko' wood has a density of 0.65 g/cm^3. Express this density in kg/m^3.
kept.explanation: To convert g/cm^3 to kg/m^3, multiply by 1000, since 1 g/cm^3 = 1000 kg/m^3. So 0.65 g/cm^3 x 1000 = 650 kg/m^3.
kept.pidgin: To change g/cm^3 to kg/m^3, you go multiply by 1000 because 1 g/cm^3 = 1000 kg/m^3. So 0.65 x 1000 = 650 kg/m^3.

kept.q: In fluid mechanics, the terminal velocity v of a small sphere falling through a viscous fluid is given by v = 2r^2(rho - sigma)g / (9 x eta), where r is the radius of the sphere, rho and sigma are densities, g is acceleration due to gravity, and eta is the coefficient of viscosity. Using dimensional analysis on this equation, what is the dimension of eta in terms of [M], [L] and [T]?
kept.explanation: Make eta the subject: eta = 2r^2(rho - sigma)g / (9v). The dimensions are r^2 = [L]^2, density = [M][L]^-3, g = [L][T]^-2, and v = [L][T]^-1. Multiplying the numerator gives [M][T]^-2 (the L powers cancel: 2 - 3 + 1 = 0), then dividing by v's dimension [L][T]^-1 gives [M][L]^-1[T]^-1, which matches the known unit of viscosity (Pa.s = kg/m/s).
kept.pidgin: Make eta be the subject: eta = 2r^2(rho-sigma)g / (9v). r^2 na [L]^2, density na [M][L]^-3, g na [L][T]^-2, v na [L][T]^-1. If you multiply the top one, the L powers cancel (2-3+1=0) make e remain [M][T]^-2, then divide by v's [L][T]^-1 e go give [M][L]^-1[T]^-1, wey be the correct viscosity dimension.
